expected_symptom: Both [unroll]-marked loops survive as structured SPIR-V loops with back-edges instead of being flattened.
summary: Nested [unroll] loops still emit surviving OpLoopMerge back-edges under -spirv on main and on all 19 stable releases that have a SPIR-V backend (v1.5.2010 onward; v1.4.1907 answers SPIR-V CodeGen not available, so history is only checkable that far). Nesting is not the blocker: the same nest with a constant inner bound unrolls completely. The blocker is the inner trip count depending on the outer induction variable, which leaves neither level inner-most with a known bound, the only shape SPIRV-Tools loop_unroller.cpp:1113 can unroll. Separately, the SPIR-V path exits 0 in silence on an [unroll] it cannot honour where the DXIL path hard-errors.
title: [SPIR-V] Nested static 'for' loops with unroll translate to 'while( true )' loops with actual branches
